subject: MAP: Technical evaluation plan - Acme (next steps)
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap + MAP (technical evaluation milestone)

Hi Alex — great to meet earlier. Quick recap from our discovery and the next steps we discussed on the call, plus an initial MAP draft attached (Acme_MAP_draft_v1.pdf).

Summary: Acme wants predictable latency and cost for chat-like agent workflows (RAG + multi-turn). High level success criteria we sketched: p95 latency under 250ms for 1-2k context for single-turn replies (lower is better), and unit cost target ~<$0.20 per 1k tokens in production (we'll refine with quantization/batching).

Proposed MAP milestone: Technical evaluation plan (this message focuses on this milestone). Draft milestones (dates are target/placeholder):
- 2026-06-22: Acme shares representative evaluation dataset and 3 canonical prompts for benchmarking (owner: Acme)
- 2026-06-30: Redwood runs benchmark suite (latency, throughput, cost profile) across shortlisted model variants (owner: Redwood / Marissa)
- 2026-07-07: Joint quality review (human eval + automated metrics) and selection of preferred model/config (owner: Acme + Redwood)
- 2026-07-20: Finalize deployment config (batching, quantization profile, routing policy) and pricing proposal (owner: Redwood)
- 2026-07-30: Target contract signature / go-ahead (owner: Acme + Redwood)

Benchmark success criteria (draft):
- Latency: p95 < 250ms for short responses (100-300 token outputs) on a Dedicated test instance at expected concurrency (2-4 qps sustained)
- Cost: baseline <$0.20 per 1k output tokens (estimated with quantized 8-bit kernels and batching)
- Quality: >=85% pass rate on Acme-provided scoring rubric (3 human raters or equivalent automated scores)

Model shortlist (initial):
- Llama 3 70B (quantized 8-bit)
- Mistral-Instruct-8B (optimized)
- Falcon-40B-Instruct
- Redwood-Open-3B (lightweight baseline)

Dependencies: access to representative data, a short-term test key / sandbox account, and confirmation on procurement timeline (procurement may request SOW/pricing).

Ask from Acme for this milestone:
1) Send 10-20 representative prompts + 15 representative doc contexts (redacted ok) by 2026-06-22
2) Confirm a test account or IP allowlist for Redwood to run benchmarks against Dedicated test pool

I'll attach the MAP draft and a benchmark template (spreadsheet) in a follow-up. Marissa (cc) will lead the bench runs. Please let me know if the timeline looks feasible on your side and who else from Acme should be involved (procurement/SRE).

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Subject: Re: Post-call recap + MAP (technical evaluation milestone)

Thanks Camila — that aligns with our conversation. Priya (SRE) and I will pull together representative prompts and sample contexts; target to share by EOD 2026-06-22. A few quick clarifications:

1) For latency targets, can you confirm whether the p95 < 250ms assumes a single-stream (no batching) or includes your recommended batching profile?
2) For the test environment, we prefer Redwood to run the bench on a sandbox Dedicated instance in our region (us-west). Can Marissa share exact test endpoints and any network/IP allowlist we need to configure?
3) Procurement will need a rough estimate of monthly committed capacity and a preliminary SOW to speed approvals. Can you include a ballpark in the MAP doc?

We can loop in procurement after we have benchmark results and the rough pricing.

Appreciate the clear milestone list — looks good.

—Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Product Engineering | Acme Corp
alex.johnson@acme.com
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-18T11:10:00-07:00
Subject: MAP draft + benchmark template (attached)

Thanks Alex — tagging responses inline:

1) Latency assumption: p95 < 250ms is for a near-production config (continuous batching + KV cache disabled for cold-start worst-case). We'll include two operating points in the bench report: 
  - Single-request (minimal batching) p95 target
  - Production-ish (continuous batching + prefix caching) expected p95

2) Marissa will share endpoints and an allowlist spec. For the Dedicated sandbox we typically provide a GPU-backed pool in us-west and a short-lived access token for the bench runs.

3) We'll include a conservative committed capacity estimate and an SOW template in the MAP doc. Ballpark example (placeholder): monthly reserved capacity equivalent to 4 vGPU instances, with burst credits for 30% excess. We'll refine after bench results.

Attached: Acme_MAP_draft_v1.pdf (includes milestone table and owner column) and benchmark_results_template.xlsx (spreadsheet you can populate). Also linking a HubSpot record with the deal notes.

Next steps:
- Acme: upload sample prompts + contexts to the sheet / share Drive by 2026-06-22
- Redwood (Marissa): provision sandbox and run baseline bench by 2026-06-30

I'll update the MAP milestone table with the dates we agreed and keep procurement notes in the SOW section.

Camila
Attachment: benchmark_results_template.xlsx
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-06-18T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP draft + benchmark template (attached)

Hey team — I'll own the bench execution. Quick note on setup and what I'll need from Acme:

Planned bench config (baseline):
- Test infra: Redwood dedicated sandbox (us-west) — single 80GB A100 equivalent for the large model runs, 1-2x 48GB GPUs for mid-size models.
- Workload shapes: 1) short-chat (user prompt -> 100-300 token reply), 2) RAG summarization (2k token context + 200 token output), 3) batch summarization (50 concurrent short jobs).
- Metrics collected: p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput, GPU utilization, estimated token cost (based on per-second GPU cost + token accounting), and quality scores (human + automated).

What I need from Acme by 2026-06-22:
- 10-20 canonical prompts (spread across the three workload shapes)
- 10-15 representative context docs (redacted ok)
- Priority signal: which workload shape is most common in production (chat vs. long-context RAG)

If you prefer, we can run an initial synthetic pass with standard prompts to get an early read while you assemble the representative data. I'll also prepare runbooks and a small harness so you can reproduce runs locally if needed.

PR on constraints: if Acme needs p95 <150ms at 4 qps sustained for the 2k-context workload we may need a larger committed capacity or model distillation — we'll document tradeoffs in the MAP.

I'll provision sandbox access later today and post the endpoints + allowlist IPs in this thread once ready.

—Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks — looking forward to the bench results.
